entries.title: Small bird
entries.summary: A small brown bird that lives in a tree, perches on crowns and lamp heads, and wanders over the square between perches.

declared.band: It flies between 3 m and 10 m above the ground: above the society's 1.9 m walker capsule with a metre to spare, so it never flies through a person, and below the flight module's 12 m ceiling. It turns to land 1 m above a perch, two grid cells, so the column it descends is checked cell by cell.
declared.body: A small garden bird authored for this repository, about 200 mm from beak to tail: legs 32 mm high, a body 140 mm long and 60 mm round, a 46 mm head, a short beak and a flat tail. Declared for this catalog; not measured from any bird.
declared.presentation: Drawn banking at most 45 degrees into a turn, with a wingbeat of 120 ms while it flaps. The step never reads either; they are how the renderer draws what the step hands it.
declared.size: 280 mm from wingtip to wingtip, the span its body and two wings draw: the wing hinge 30 mm out from the body's centre and a wing 110 mm long, twice over.
declared.speeds: It cruises at 5 m/s, at most 8 m/s, and glides in level flight at 4.5 m/s or faster; it changes speed by at most 6 m/s each second and turns at most 3 radians a second. Declared so a loop over a 24 m square lasts several seconds and a turn reads as a bird's; not measured from any bird.
declared.texels: Its maps are embedded at 64 texels a side, an eighth of the 512 texel sets it is dressed in: a bird is a few centimetres on screen at the distances a square is watched from, so its maps stay small.
declared.times: It stays on a perch 8 to 30 seconds and wanders 6 to 20 seconds; when a perch ends, half its choices wander before choosing another perch and half fly straight to one. Declared so a square with a few birds always has one in the air.
declared.vertical: It climbs at most 2 m/s and descends at most 2.5 m/s while flying, takes off up its perch's column at 1.5 m/s and lands down it at 1 m/s, a second to land from its approach height.
declared.wing: One flat wing 110 mm long and 60 mm wide, hinged 30 mm out from the body's centre line at the top of its shoulders; the renderer draws it on both sides, turned half a turn about the vertical for the left.

entries.reason: The first flying kind: a small bird that shows flight over a world a person built, taking off from and landing on the perches its objects declare. A larger flyer is another entry with its own figures, never code.
